issues.title: [P0] HR-OS5 Phase 0 – Foundation & Cleanup
issues.body:
Summary:

Phase 0 focuses on cleaning up the model, centralizing configuration, and consolidating Dynamixel and teleop basics. The goal is to have a clean, reproducible foundation before expanding capabilities.

Goals:
- hros5_description is structurally correct and mesh-complete
- DXL configs centralized in YAML
- joint_limits.yaml exists and matches servo ranges
- Head teleop is clean and reliable
- Core helper tooling exists in hros5_utils

Child tasks:
- [P0] hros5_description: verify hros5.xacro as top-level
- [P0] hros5_description: cleanup component xacros
- [P0] hros5_description: add missing mesh and collision geometry
- [P0] hros5_control: create joint_limits.yaml
- [P0] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: create dxl_bus.yaml
- [P0] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: split servo configs by body part
- [P0] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: ensure DXL nodes load YAML configs
- [P0] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: move all DXL nodes into bridge package
- [P0] hros5_teleop: validate head teleop node and launch
- [P0] hros5_utils: add compile_commands generation helper
- [P0] hros5_utils: add basic DXL tooling scripts
- [P0] hros5_head_tracker_cpp: finalize head_params.yaml

Acceptance Criteria:
- All P0 issues are created and closed
- Workspace can build and run minimal head + hands control reliably

issues.title: [P1] HR-OS5 Phase 1 – Full Manual Teleop Control
issues.body:
Summary:

Phase 1 focuses on achieving reliable manual control of head, hands, and arms using the PS4 controller. The goal is to be able to move all upper body joints from teleop.

Goals:
- Hands and arms can be controlled via PS4
- Standard ps4_mapping.yaml exists
- Basic bringup launch for minimal hardware stack

Child tasks:
- [P1] hros5_description: validate joint limits in URDF
- [P1] hros5_control: create controllers.yaml
- [P1] hros5_control: create hardware_params.yaml
- [P1] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: add diagnostics publisher
- [P1] hros5_teleop: add hands_teleop_node
- [P1] hros5_teleop: add arms_teleop_node for joint stepping
- [P1] hros5_teleop: create ps4_mapping.yaml
- [P1] hros5_teleop: create deadzones and speed scales config
- [P1] hros5_head_tracker_cpp: ensure output topic is consistent
- [P1] hros5_bringup: create hros5_minimal.launch.py
- [P1] hros5_utils: add joint state snapshot/report helper

Acceptance Criteria:
- All P1 issues are created and closed
- Operator can control head + both hands + arms via PS4 controller

issues.title: [P2] HR-OS5 Phase 2 – Digital Twin (Gazebo + MoveIt2)
issues.body:
Summary:

Phase 2 focuses on building a full digital twin in simulation. HR-OS5 should spawn in Gazebo Harmonic with controllers and be usable in MoveIt2.

Goals:
- Gazebo launch works with full robot
- Sim ros2_control controllers are configured
- MoveIt2 config package exists and can plan for arms and legs
- Perception stub package exists for future use

Child tasks:
- [P2] hros5_description: add inertias and masses
- [P2] hros5_perception: create stub package
- [P2] hros5_gazebo: create hros5_gazebo.launch.py
- [P2] hros5_gazebo: add sim_controllers.yaml
- [P2] hros5_gazebo: add empty_room.world
- [P2] hros5_gazebo: add IMU plugin
- [P2] hros5_gazebo: add foot contact sensor plugins
- [P2] hros5_moveit_config: generate initial MoveIt config
- [P2] hros5_moveit_config: define MoveIt groups
- [P2] hros5_bringup: create hros5_simulation_full.launch.py

Acceptance Criteria:
- All P2 issues are created and closed
- Full robot can be spawned and controlled in simulation

issues.title: [P3] HR-OS5 Phase 3 – IK Framework
issues.body:
Summary:

Phase 3 introduces FK/IK support and endpoint control. The goal is to command end-effector positions instead of raw joint angles.

Goals:
- IK skeleton for arms and legs exists
- Endpoint teleop node can request IK solutions
- Behaviors and perception interfaces are defined

Child tasks:
- [P3] hros5_control: add IK skeleton files
- [P3] hros5_control: define IK interfaces (topics/services)
- [P3] hros5_teleop: implement endpoint_control_node
- [P3] hros5_teleop: create endpoint_limits.yaml
- [P3] hros5_perception: define target pose topics
- [P3] hros5_behaviors: create package skeleton
- [P3] hros5_bringup: create hros5_full_hardware.launch.py
- [P3] hros5_moveit_config: tune kinematics.yaml

Acceptance Criteria:
- All P3 issues are created and closed
- Arms can be controlled via end-effector targets (in sim and/or hardware)

issues.title: [P4] HR-OS5 Phase 4 – Balance & Standing
issues.body:
Summary:

Phase 4 focuses on standing balance: COM estimation, ZMP control, and ankle/torso compensation. The goal is to have HR-OS5 stand stably under its own weight.

Child tasks:
- [P4] hros5_control: add balance framework
- [P4] hros5_behaviors: integrate balance modules into walking pipeline

Acceptance Criteria:
- All P4 issues are created and closed
- Robot can stand in place with active balance control (at least in simulation)

issues.title: [P5] HR-OS5 Phase 5 – Static Walking
issues.body:
Summary:

Phase 5 adds a static walking engine: step planning, foot trajectories, and a walking state machine. The goal is slow, stable walking.

Child tasks:
- [P5] hros5_control: add gait/trajectory generators
- [P5] hros5_behaviors: implement walking state machine and step planner

Acceptance Criteria:
- All P5 issues are created and closed
- Robot can perform slow, stable walking in simulation and initial hardware tests

issues.title: [P6] HR-OS5 Phase 6 – Autonomous Walking Demo
issues.body:
Summary:

Phase 6 integrates perception, behaviors, and bringup into a full autonomous walking demo.

Child tasks:
- [P6] hros5_behaviors: implement autonomous behaviors (walk_to_point, follow_person, demo scripts)
- [P6] hros5_bringup: create hros5_autonomous_demo.launch.py

Acceptance Criteria:
- All P6 issues are created and closed
- Single launch brings up an autonomous walking demo

issues.title: [P0] hros5_description: verify hros5.xacro as top-level
issues.body:
Summary:
Ensure that `urdf/hros5.xacro` is the true top-level model file and that all component xacros resolve correctly via `robot/robot.xacro`.

Tasks:
- Verify includes for head.xacro, arms.xacro, torso.xacro, legs.xacro, hands.xacro
- Confirm no missing macro arguments
- Run xacro CLI for full validation
- Update include paths if needed

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running `xacro hros5.xacro` produces a valid URDF
- No errors or warnings from missing macros
- All body parts included in correct tree position

Testing Notes:
- Run: `cd hros5_description/urdf && xacro hros5.xacro > test.urdf`

issues.title: [P0] hros5_description: cleanup component xacros
issues.body:
Summary:
Ensure component xacros (head, arms, legs, hands, torso) contain only kinematic structure and visuals/collisions. All ros2_control elements must be in `hros5_control.xacro`.

Tasks:
- Remove `<transmission>` tags from component xacros
- Remove any ros2_control-specific `<gazebo>` plugin tags
- Keep joint/link structure intact
- Move any leftover hardwareInterface tags into `hros5_control.xacro`

Acceptance Criteria:
- Component xacros contain only kinematics and visuals/collisions
- ros2_control loads correctly from `hros5_control.xacro`

Testing Notes:
- Re-generate URDF and visually inspect
- Optionally check with urdf.robotsfan.com

issues.title: [P0] hros5_description: add missing mesh and collision geometry
issues.body:
Summary:
Replace placeholder geometry with real STL/DAE meshes for hands, legs, and feet. Add missing collision meshes for robust collision checking.

Tasks:
- Add real STL meshes for hand and finger links
- Add STL/DAE meshes for feet if missing
- Create or import collision meshes for hands and feet
- Update xacros to reference these meshes

Acceptance Criteria:
- RViz displays all hands and feet with real meshes
- Collision geometry is visible for hands and feet in URDF tools

Testing Notes:
- Launch display_hros5 launch file and inspect visuals and collisions

issues.title: [P0] hros5_control: create joint_limits.yaml
issues.body:
Summary:
Create a single `config/joint_limits.yaml` file that centralizes joint limits for all robot joints, consistent with URDF and Dynamixel capabilities.

Tasks:
- Create `config/joint_limits.yaml`
- Populate position, velocity, and effort limits per joint
- Cross-check against URDF and servo specs
- Plan for reuse by MoveIt config later

Acceptance Criteria:
- ros2_control loads joint_limits.yaml without warnings
- Limits match URDF definitions and known servo ranges

Testing Notes:
- Start ros2_control and inspect logs for limit-related warnings

issues.title: [P0] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: create dxl_bus.yaml
issues.body:
Summary:
Centralize Dynamixel bus configuration (device, baudrate, protocol, timeouts) into `config/dxl_bus.yaml`.

Tasks:
- Create `config/dxl_bus.yaml`
- Add parameters: device path, baudrate, protocol version
- Add optional timeout/retry parameters
- Update dxl nodes to read these parameters instead of hardcoding

Acceptance Criteria:
- All DXL nodes read bus configuration from YAML
- No hardcoded device or baudrate values remain in code

Testing Notes:
- Run a dxl node with `--ros-args --params-file config/dxl_bus.yaml` and verify behavior

issues.title: [P0] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: split servo configs by body part
issues.body:

Organize servo ID and limit configuration per body part using separate YAML files.

- Create `config/arm_servos.yaml`

- Move ID, offset, and limit information into these files
- Update DXL nodes to load the correct config for their body part

Acceptance Criteria:
- Servo IDs and limits are no longer hardcoded in C++
- Each DXL node loads from the appropriate YAML file

Testing Notes:
- Start each DXL node and confirm parameters are loaded from YAML

issues.title: [P0] hros5_dynamixel_bridge: ensure DXL nodes load YAML configs

Ensure that all Dynamixel nodes obtain their configuration (bus + servo IDs + limits) from YAML rather than hardcoded values.
